what: Madrigal sells Rezdiffra, the first drug approved in the United States for MASH, a form of fatty liver disease with scarring that affects millions of people and previously had no approved treatment.
customers: Hepatologists and endocrinologists treating fatty liver disease, paid for by insurers and Medicare.
moat: First approval in a disease with no other approved drug, with the clinical data and prescriber relationships that come from getting there first.
risks: A $156M net loss and negative free cash flow as the launch is funded
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly are developing GLP-1 drugs for the same disease with enormous resources
opportunities: Revenue went from $180M to $958M in a year and is $1.4B over the last twelve months: one of the fastest drug launches on record
Analysts see about 74% upside, with 18 covering the stock, and most diagnosed MASH patients are still untreated
watch: Quarterly Rezdiffra prescriptions and the data from competing GLP-1 trials in MASH.
